City Through the Lens: Mexico City, Mexico

Local videographers reveal how they film their hometown — the real locations, permit hurdles, and techniques you won't find in guidebooks.

🎬 Local videographer interview coming soon — subscribe on YouTube to see it first

Quick Takeaways for Filmmakers

  • Best filming season: Highland subtropical; dry Nov-Apr, wet May-Oct
  • Top 3 landmarks: Zócalo & Metropolitan Cathedral, Teotihuacán Pyramids, Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul)
  • Main airport: Benito Juárez
  • Drone rules: need SEDENA approval.
  • Featured camera: Canon EOS R6 II

3 Must-Film Locations in Mexico City

1. Zócalo & Metropolitan Cathedral

Filming Tip: Largest cathedral Americas; sinking angle; plaza events; drone banned.

2. Teotihuacán Pyramids

Filming Tip: Sun/Moon pyramids; climb early; 50km from city; tour or bus.

3. Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul)

Filming Tip: Coyoacán neighborhood; book weeks ahead; no interior photography.

Weather Reality Check

Highland subtropical; dry Nov-Apr, wet May-Oct. Mild year-round.

Pro tip: Plan your shoot dates around these conditions. The "best" months mean better light, fewer crowds, and more predictable weather windows.

Airport Transfer & Arrival Tips

Benito Juárez (MEX) 30-60min metro/Uber.

Factor in transfer time when booking flights. Arriving early gives you buffer for gear checks and acclimatization before shooting.

Permits, Rules & Local Etiquette

Archaeological zones rules. Museums strict. Drones need SEDENA approval.

Remember: Always ask before filming people, especially in religious or residential areas. Respect local customs — it's the difference between getting great footage and being asked to delete it.
